fact: 阿根廷的货币局（Caja de Conversión）直到1929年仍以纸币兑换黄金。1929年大萧条冲击出口后，阿根廷于1929年12月放弃金本位，比多数国家更早；比索随之贬值，对出口商构成缓冲，但推高了进口品价格。1935年货币局被彻底关闭，中央银行依1935年3月陆续颁布的第12155至12160号法律设立，同年6月开业，首任行长劳尔·普雷维什。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Infamous Decade（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: He also ordered the definitive closure of the Currency Board (Caja de Conversión), which until 1929 had exchanged paper money for gold. To replace it as a tool for exchange rate control, he consulted the Bank of England, which sent one of its directors, Otto Niemeyer, to Buenos Aires. ... Laws 12,155 to 12,160, enacted successively in March 1935; the Central Bank opened in June of that year, headed by Raúl Prebisch.

sources.title: Grokipedia, 1930s in Argentina
sources.quote: A key mitigating factor was Argentina's early abandonment of the gold standard in December 1929, which enabled peso devaluation and monetary accommodation, averting the deflationary spiral seen elsewhere and facilitating a nascent recovery by 1933.

fact: 1930年9月6日，乌里布鲁将军率少量部队进入布宜诺斯艾利斯，几乎未遇实质抵抗即控制玫瑰宫，伊里戈延政府被推翻，政变本身无死亡。政变后宪法被中止、政党被禁、选举被暂停，乌里布鲁提出按职团主义与法西斯模式重组国家，阿根廷进入持续13年的「臭名昭著的十年」。政变的支持基础在1929年大萧条后形成：伊里戈延为压缩开支削减政府服务，失业加速，政治支持流失；反对党在1928年与1930年的国会选举中获胜，1930年8月9日与8月20日两批反对派先后正式抗议其统治。

sources.title: Wikipedia, 1930 Argentine coup d'état（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: The coup took place on 6 September 1930 when Uriburu led a small detachment of troops into the capital, experiencing no substantial opposition and taking control of the Casa Rosada. ... There were no casualties in the coup. ... With the onset of the Great Depression in 1929 that impacted Argentina, Yrigoyen lost political support as he retrenched government services which resulted in acceleration of unemployment.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Infamous Decade（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: The Infamous Decade (Spanish: Década Infame) was a period in Argentine history that began with the 1930 coup d'état against President Hipólito Yrigoyen. ... this period was characterized by the persecution of the political opposition (mainly against the UCR) and generalized government corruption, against the background of the Great Depression.

fact: 1929至1933年，阿根廷主要出口品（谷物、亚麻籽、肉类）的批发价格下跌约一半；以1937年为100的贸易条件指数，1928年为97.6，1931年降至63.2。出口收入同步萎缩：1932年进口实物量仅为1929年的40%。这意味着以出口部门为生的人在1929—1931年经历的是收入腰斩，而不是物价上涨。

sources.title: The Cambridge History of Latin America, Vol. VIII, Argentina 1930–46（Rock）
sources.quote: From 1929 to 1933 the wholesale prices of Argentina's major exports - grains, linseed and meat declined by roughly half. Real wages fell by an estimated 10 per cent. ... terms of trade, taking 1937 as base 100, stood at 97.6 in 1928 but only 63.2 in 1931. ... By 1932 imports by volume stood at scarcely 40 per cent of the 1929 figure.

sources.title: Uniflection, Chapter 10 Imperialism, Colonial Economies, and the Global Periphery
sources.quote: The Great Depression collapsed wheat and beef prices in the world market by roughly half between 1929 and 1932; Argentine export earnings fell by similar magnitude.

fact: 与出口部门的崩塌相比，阿根廷城市失业在萧条初期出奇地轻：可见失业率约5%—6%；1933年英国驻布宜诺斯艾利斯商务参赞估算仅2.8%，其继任者1934年称「与世界上其他地方相比，阿根廷可以说没有严重的失业问题」。但官方统计可能严重低估真实失业，且实际工资下跌约10%。城市中的食品饮料、冶金与小型家用杂货业受冲击，建筑业与纺织业基本未受影响。

sources.title: The Cambridge History of Latin America, Vol. VIII, Argentina 1930–46（Rock）
sources.quote: In the cities the depression struck the food and drink, the metallurgical and the small-householdgoods industries, but left construction and especially textiles unscathed. Visible unemployment remained remarkably light, at perhaps 5 to 6 per cent. In 1933 the British commercial attache in Buenos Aires calculated unemployment at a mere 2.8 per cent. ... Real wages fell by an estimated 10 per cent.

fact: 为应对国际收支危机，阿根廷在1931年10月效仿多国实施外汇管制；1931年引入所得税，以降低对关税收入的依赖；同时提高进口关税，使关税从财政收入工具转变为贸易管制工具。1930年公共开支为9.34亿比索，1932年削减至6.48亿比索，公共行政部门裁员约2万人，激进党人被列为主要对象。

sources.title: The Cambridge History of Latin America, Vol. VIII, Argentina 1930–46（Rock）
sources.quote: In an effort to curb imports the Uriburu government raised tariffs, which now became more important as trade regulators than as instruments of taxation. ... In October 1931, following the example of numerous other countries, Argentina imposed exchange controls. ... the government raised taxes and in 1931 introduced an income tax that aimed to lessen dependence on tariff duties as a source of public finance. ... spending, which fell from 934 million pesos in 1930 to 648 million in 1932. Massive lay-offs among the personnel of the public administration — about twenty thousand in all — became the chief weapon in the fight to reduce spending, Radicals being the main victims.

fact: 1930年9月6日政变后，乌里布鲁禁止政党、暂停选举并中止1853年宪法；他提出按职团主义与法西斯路线重组国家。此后13年的「臭名昭著的十年」以镇压反对派（主要针对激进公民联盟）、政治腐败与选举舞弊为特征，1931年4月的选举在激进党获胜后被宣布无效。对居住者而言，这意味着政治身份本身成为风险：党员身份、工会身份或报刊立场都可能招致拘押与失权。

sources.title: Wikipedia, 1930 Argentine coup d'état（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: In the aftermath of the coup, major changes to Argentinean politics and government took place, with Uriburu banning political parties, suspending elections, and suspending the 1853 Constitution. Uriburu proposed that Argentina be reorganized along corporatist and fascist lines. The coup marked the start of the Infamous Decade, a 13-year period during which the military ruled Argentina through repression, political corruption and electoral fraud.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Infamous Decade（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: Uriburu had publicly committed himself to calling free elections as soon as possible; these took place in April 1931 and, to the surprise of the dictator's allies, gave victory to the Yrigoyenist radical Honorio Pueyrredón. Radicalism had clearly not disappeared, but the government had decreed its extinction, and therefore annulled the elections.

fact: 伊里戈延政府两年支出快速增长后，1930年预算赤字达GDP的6.5%；到1931年公共债务达13亿比索，比1929年增加逾50%。收入随萧条骤降，使新政府压缩支出与增加税收的压力同时出现。1930年出口价值与出口数量（因歉收）双双下降，而进口收缩更慢、进口价格跌幅远小于出口价格，形成严重国际收支逆差并耗尽黄金储备。

sources.title: The Cambridge History of Latin America, Vol. VIII, Argentina 1930–46（Rock）
sources.quote: In 1930, after two years of rapidly growing government spending under Yrigoyen, the budget deficit had climbed to the high rate of 6.5 per cent of GDP. By 1931 the public debt had reached 1.3 billion pesos — an increase of more than 50 per cent since 1929. ... In 1930 both the value of exports and, because of harvest failures, the volume of exports fell. Imports, however, contracted more slowly, and import prices fell much less steeply than export prices

fact: 比索贬值使外资公司的黄金或硬通货利润相应缩减，许多公司因此停止向母国汇款、期待汇率回升：英资铁路公司在1930年7月至1932年7月间因此损失约600万英镑。1934年阿根廷的外国投资总额为43亿比索，其中仅9亿为公共债务，其余多为私人直接投资（铁路、公用事业、银行）。这意味着1929—1932年间，英资在阿根廷的资产既无法汇出利润，也难以出售变现。

sources.title: The Cambridge History of Latin America, Vol. VIII, Argentina 1930–46（Rock）
sources.quote: the depreciation of the peso provoked a corresponding contraction in the gold or hard currency profits of foreign companies, many of which therefore ceased making remittances abroad in the hope that exchange rates would eventually improve. The British railway companies, for example, lost an estimated £6 million in this way between July 1930 and July 1932. ... out of a total foreign investment of 4.3 billion pesos in 1934, only 900 million constituted public debts.

fact: 1929年阿根廷人均GDP约为美国水平的63%，是英国资本、意大利与西班牙移民与潘帕斯出口腹地共同支撑的移民型经济体。英国资本修建的铁路把小麦从潘帕斯运到布宜诺斯艾利斯出口，冷藏船自1880年代起使新鲜牛肉可销往伦敦。这种「初级产品—铁路—冷藏航运」的组合是1929年阿根廷的产业骨架，也是它在1929—1932年价格腰斩时毫无缓冲的原因。

sources.title: Uniflection, Chapter 10 Imperialism, Colonial Economies, and the Global Periphery
sources.quote: By 1929, Argentina's per-capita GDP had reached roughly 63 percent of US levels, a settler economy with British capital, Italian and Spanish labor, and a Pampas hinterland producing for the Atlantic market. ... Refrigerated shipping, demonstrated commercially in the 1870s and at industrial scale by the 1880s, made fresh Argentine beef saleable in London. British capital financed the railways that hauled wheat from the Pampas to Buenos Aires for export.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Economy of Argentina（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: Early in the 20th century, Argentina's per capita GDP ranked among the top 10 globally, at par with Canada and Australia and ahead of France and Italy. ... From 1880–1905, British and French investments fueled livestock and grain exports, sparking rapid expansion and mass European immigration.

fact: 1933年《罗加—朗西曼协定》为阿根廷争取到每年39万吨的对英牛肉配额，代价是阿根廷在关税、煤炭关税与铁路运价上作出让步，并把布宜诺斯艾利斯公共运输的控制权交给英资的运输公司（Corporación de Transportes）；协定同时规定85%的出口须交由英国冷藏船公司安排。该协定在阿根廷被民族主义者广泛批评为不对称的让步。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Infamous Decade（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: …390,000 tons of meat per year were allotted to Argentina in exchange for many concessions to British companies, and 85% of exportation had to be arranged through British refrigerated shippers. … given control over the public transport in Buenos Aires to a British company, the Corporación de Transportes. … In addition, the tariffs of the railways operated by the UK were not regulated, the treaty did not establish customs fees over coal, had given special dispensation to British companies with investments in Argentina and had reduced the prices of their exports.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Economy of Argentina（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: The Roca–Runciman Treaty (1933), negotiated to preserve Argentine beef access to British markets following the Ottawa Conference, was widely criticized by Argentine nationalists as an asymmetrical concession to British commercial interests.
